channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Instacart to Wind Down Smart Cart Business Amid Sale Talks
item.description: Instacart will stop offering high-tech shopping carts to grocers, its first announced strategy shift since reports emerged that the company is in talks to sell itself.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung

item.title: Intel to Buy Israeli Startup Classiq in Quantum Computing Push
item.description: Intel Corp. agreed to buy Israeli startup Classiq Technologies Ltd. as part of a push to capitalize on quantum computing, a still-nascent field that is seeking commercial applications.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: France Offers Students Funding, Reforms to Try to End Protests
item.description: The French government plans to increase the number of third-level student places and make €4 billion ($4.5 billion) available for high-school renovations as it tries to end nationwide protests that have turned violent in recent weeks.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Berthelot

item.title: Tesla-SpaceX Merger Hopes Send Sell Ratings to 11-Year Low
item.description: Tesla Inc. analysts are rapidly turning more bullish on the electric carmaker’s stock as a long awaited combination with SpaceX edges closer to reality.
item.dc:creator: Jordan Fitzgerald

item.title: Anthropic Drops Its S-1, Giving Market Glimpse Into Finances
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow takes a look at Anthropic's regulatory filing as the company prepares to go public under the ticker ANT. The S-1 revealed Anthropic's revenue and spending, along with its plan for an unusual corporate structure. Plus, venture investors are in line for a big payday when Anthropic goes public. Matt Murphy from Menlo Ventures and Byron Deeter from Bessemer Venture Partners discuss what they think happens next for the AI market. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic’s S-1 Reveals Financial War Chest
item.description: Anthropic’s S-1 filing shows it’s not going public out of desperation but, in fact, has a financial war chest, explains Gil Luria, managing director of D.A. Davidson. Luria explains why Anthropic’s structure as a public benefit corporation and its majority voting power controlled by a group of seven people make for a more complicated and unusual structure. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic to Deliver Menlo’s Biggest-Ever Return
item.description: Menlo Ventures’ investment in Anthropic will deliver the firm’s largest return ever when the AI company goes public, says partner Matt Murphy. Murphy explains why Menlo backed Anthropic in every round since 2023 and how the conversation around AI is moving beyond models to delivering compute efficiently. He discusses Anthropic’s S-1 with Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lori Keith Sees Long AI Growth as Anthropic files IPO
item.description: Discussing Anthropic’s IPO filing, portfolio manager Lori Keith described AI’s shift from pilot projects toward companies capturing measurable economic value. She said Anthropic’s customer growth signals strong demand: nearly 12,000 customers spend at least $100,000 annually, up from about 950 a year earlier, and more than 1,900 spend at least $1 million. Keith said adoption remains early, with engineering and coding among the leading uses and customer service and other applications broadening. She sees opportunities not only for AI infrastructure and chip providers, but also for downstream businesses and companies supplying power and water infrastructure. The discussion also noted a filing disclosure that one customer accounted for more than 10% of Anthropic’s revenue as of June 30. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Grows More Reliant on Google, Amazon, Microsoft
item.description: Anthropic PBC is relying more and more on Alphabet Inc.’s Google, Amazon.com Inc. and Microsoft Corp. to sell its artificial intelligence technology to customers, despite the three companies being rivals, investors and key suppliers of computing power.
item.dc:creator: Davey Alba, Rebecca Torrence and Matt Day

item.title: Anthropic Files for Massive Nasdaq IPO
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Anthropic makes it official, filing for a Nasdaq IPO in what will be one of the biggest public debuts ever. Plus, Claudia Sahm on rising inflation risks and the case for an October rate hike. Bruce Richards on AI’s next phase, and Jefferies’ Jason Greenberg on where AI spending goes next. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Building the Next Generation of Chips
item.description: Forge Nano’s CEO Paul Lichty joins Bloomberg Open Interest to discuss the company’s atomic-precision technology for semiconductors and lithium-ion batteries, its plans to expand US production and why he sees continued opportunity in AI-driven chip demand and domestic manufacturing. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Looks to Raise $95 Billion From Stock Sale to Fund AI Investments
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. is seeking to raise as much as $95 billion from selling common and preferred stock to support its development in artificial intelligence. Bloomberg's Sarah Frier reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Google Fitbit Edge Review: Smartwatch-Like Tracker Showcases Google Health
item.description: The best thing about the $180 Fitbit Edge is the Google Health app, which doesn’t actually require users to own a Fitbit.
item.dc:creator: Dana Wollman

item.title: Goldman’s Pasquariello Says Tech Rout Casts Doubt on AI Trade
item.description: Hedge funds sold technology stocks at the fastest pace in two years last Thursday during Wall Street’s biggest rout since July, casting serious doubt over conviction in the trade, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s Tony Pasquariello.
item.dc:creator: Jan-Patrick Barnert

item.title: Anthropic Files for IPO in Global Race to Raise Cash for AI
item.description: Anthropic filed for its long-awaited IPO, a landmark moment in an industry that is growing ever-hungrier for cash to power ahead. Ed Ludlow reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple’s Foldable iPhone Duo Draws Early Complaints of the Screen Cracking
item.description: The iPhone Duo, one of Apple Inc.’s biggest new products in years, is drawing a growing number of complaints from customers who say the foldable display cracked after just hours or days of use.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: Dutch Crypto Groups Warn of Sell Off Over Wealth-Tax Carveout
item.description: Dutch investors will likely ditch their cryptocurrency if the asset class is carved out of a shift to a new investor-friendly wealth tax, industry groups are warning.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Van Oosterom

item.title: Anthropic IPO: S-1 Filing Offers First Look at Claude Maker’s Finances
item.description: Anthropic PBC filed for its long-awaited IPO, a landmark moment in the artificial-intelligence industry that is growing ever-hungrier for cash to power ahead.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz and Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: What's Next After ChatGPT? Fei-Fei Li Has a Plan
item.description:
Emily Chang meets artificial intelligence pioneer Fei-Fei Li to discuss her innovations in the field, her $1 billion startup World Labs and why she thinks the future of AI lies beyond chatbots.
(Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Inside Anthropic, the $965 Billion AI Titan
item.description: Emily Chang meets Anthropic co-founders Dario and Daniela Amodei for a rare, in-depth discussion of the startup's origin story, its battles with the Pentagon and how the company says it intends to put safety first in the high-stakes AI race. (Source: Bloomberg)
